title: Transplantation of a 3D Bioprinted Patch in a Murine Model of Myocardial Infarction
protocol: Turn on and set up the stereomicroscope.
Set up the heat pad covered with an absorbent sheet.
Clean gloves, the surgical area, and tools with 70% ethanol.
Weigh the mouse to calculate the dosage of anesthesia injected by intraperitoneal route (ketamine 40 mg/kg, xylazine 5 mg/kg, atropine 0.15 mg/kg).
Inject the calculated dose of anesthesia.
Once the mouse reaches a deep plane of anesthesia, shave the ventral left side of the thorax with a trimmer.
Place the mouse in a chamber containing 2% isoflurane ensuring adequate extraction ventilation in the room.
Position the mouse supine and restrain it from its upper incisor teeth with a 3.0 suture taped to the bench.
Confirm sedation by performing a toe pinch.
Position a high-intensity illuminator above the mouse neck so that the oropharynx can be visualized.
Use a curved spatula to open the mouse's jaw.
Lift the tongue gently out of the way using another pair of spatulas or blunt forceps.
Position yourself at or slightly below eye-level with the body of the mouse for intubation.
Visualize the opening and closing of the vocal cords through the mouth.
Insert a 20 G plastic catheter when the vocal cords are open.
Transfer the intubated mouse to an operating surface equipped with a heating pad.
Connect the mouse to the ventilator, such as a MouseVent, which sets the target volume based on mouse weight automatically.
Deliver 1.5-2% isoflurane with oxygen via the ventilator.
Ensure there is a connection from an oxygen cylinder to the automatic ventilator at a flow rate of 1-2 L/min.
Check for bilateral chest rise to verify intubation.
Perform a toe pinch to verify anesthesia.
Apply opthalmic ointment, such as Puralube Vet Opthalmic Ointment, to both eyes to prevent drying out.
Secure the intubation tube with tape at the connecting site between the ventilator and breathing tube/catheter.
Cut a longer piece of tape and secure the mouse's left front foot in a slightly elevated position on the operating surface.
Tape down the other extremities of the mouse.
Clean the chest area with sterile 70% isopropanol, moving from center to periphery in a circular motion.
Clean the chest area further with povidone iodine solution, continuing in a circular motion and moving from center to periphery.
Perform another toe pinch to verify anesthesia.
Administer 0.08 mg/kg Temvet (buprenorphine) in 0.1 mL of 0.9% saline via subcutaneous injection.
Gently lift the skin approximately 5 mm to the left of the prominent xiphoid cartilage using fine-tip forceps.
Create a superomedial incision in the skin from this point upwards and towards the midline, to the level of the manubrium, using surgical scissors.
Separate the skin and muscle layers gently with curved forceps.
Open the muscle layer following the skin incision.
Make an incision in the third intercostal space, following the natural angle of the ribcage.
Gently spread apart the 3rd and 4th ribs using a retractor.
Remove the thin pericardium with forceps if the LAD is not visualized.
Push the left auricle upwards to locate the coronary arteries underneath if necessary.
Cut a ~3 mm long 3-0 silk suture and place this reinforcing 3-0 silk suture piece on top of the LAD in the same direction as the LAD.
Identify the LAD and pass a 7-0 silk suture under the LAD.
Complete two throws with the 7-0 silk suture and close it tightly passing on top of the supportive 3-0 silk suture to secure the LAD.
Complete the knot with a third throw in the opposite direction to secure it, ensuring no upward traction force is transmitted to the suture.
Carefully move the bioprinted patch from a six well plate to the infarct area by using the sterile inside surface of an opened surgical scalpel packet.

Carefully position the bioprinted patch onto the anterior epicardial surface, where it should cover the whole surface and drape over the inferior and lateral edges, covering the left ventricle and the infarct zone (blanched area).
Gently close and remove the retractor without directing sharp edges towards the heart.
Use 6-0 prolene sutures in a simple interrupted pattern to close the ribcage and the muscle layers.
Inflate lungs to remove excess air in the pleural cavity while closing the chest with 6-0 prolene sutures.
Ensure the chest is tightly sealed.
Decrease isoflurane concentration to 1.0%.
Close skin with 6-0 prolene sutures in a simple interrupted pattern.
Turn off the isoflurane vaporizer.
Apply 2 mg/mL bupivacaine in 0.9% saline topically to the incision.
Administer antisedan (atipamezole) at 1 mg/kg.
Administer lasix (furosemide) at 8 mg/kg.
Inject 600 µL of 0.9% saline solution subcutaneously.
Monitor the mouse for independent breathing before removing from intubation tube.
Place mouse in a clean recovery cage on a heat pad when bilateral breathing is adequate and responds to toe pinch.
Provide the mouse with moist food, a water bottle, and nutrient/hydrating gel.
Monitor for an exaggerated breathing effort, excessive bleeding, or other potentially life-threatening complications.
Administer 0.08 mg/kg Temvet in 0.1 mL of 0.9% saline via subcutaneous or intraperitoneal injection twice daily for the first three days following the procedure.
Administer 0.08 mg/kg Temvet once daily from day four to day five following the procedure.
House mice in pairs separated by cage dividers.
Monitor mice at least daily until the end of the experiments (28 days).
Pay close attention to their wellbeing and increase monitoring frequency if there are any concerns.
